newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SWINE FEVER MAY SPREAD FURTHER IN BELGIUM.
newsitem.headline: SWINE FEVER MAY SPREAD FURTHER IN BELGIUM.

text.p: Tuesday's outbreak of swine fever in Belgium has spread from one farm to six and contamination of others is very likely, Belgian Agriculture Minister Karel Pinxten said on Thursday.
Belgium, a large producer of pork-based products, has already started an extensive slaughter programme to contain the highly contagious disease in the north of the country.
But, Pinxten said, "I would be hugely amazed if we could limit this to five, six, seven farms. That would mean there had not been any other contacts which could cause contamination."
Initial investigations pointed to a Dutch haulage firm which had transported diseased pigs from the Netherlands to Belgium, or had used infected lorries to collect Belgian pigs.
"There has been some form of carelessness," Pinxten said. Investigators were still checking routes taken by Dutch transport firms amd farms along the way.
A swine fever outbreak devastated the pig market in the Netherlands, where it has so far affected almost 300 farms and led to the destruction of some three million pigs.
Belgium has about seven million pigs.
